known_facts_book1: The fairy Ruler of all the Land of Oz, whose authority comes from the Fairy Queen **Lurline**, of whose band she was a member when Lurline made Oz a Fairyland and left her behind to rule it.
Goes to the Skeezer Country out of **duty**: having learned of the war from Glinda's Book of Records, she says she would not be doing her duty if she kept away and let her subjects fight.
Refuses to send the Wizard with threats, and refuses an escort, because Glinda argues her one unequalled art is winning hearts, which she can use better alone than with a train of followers.
Carries only a small **silver wand** tipped with a great sparkling emerald — fairies use no chemicals, herbs or wizards' tools — and it is her one weapon of offence and defence.
Says plainly she is not all-powerful: her magic is fairy magic, not sorcery or wizardry; Glinda knows arts she does not, and even the little Wizard can do things she cannot.
Argues to Dorothy that a world where every wish could be waved into being would bring weariness, not happiness, because nothing would be difficult and nothing worth earning.
Escapes the Su-dic by making herself and Dorothy **invisible** with her wand and simply walking out — the Su-dic realises too late that he knew how to undo invisibility.
Enchants Lady Aurex's house with a circle drawn by her wand so that Coo-ee-oh, who can hear every whisper on the island, cannot hear a word spoken inside it.
Is imprisoned under the lake for the whole middle of the book and cannot raise the island: Coo-ee-oh's magic is witchcraft, not fairy magic, and requires spoken words known only to her.
Takes possession of Coo-ee-oh's palace, promises the Skeezers she will try to save them, and tells them to go home and do their daily tasks with patience.
Speaks the syllable **'Oh-h-h!'** over the burning Gaulau powder, and it is her voice that raises the island.
Lets the Skeezers **elect** their own Queen, who is subject to her in turn, and they choose Lady Aurex.
Judges the Flathead people less to blame than their Dictator, and ends the book saying it is always wise to do one's duty, however unpleasant the duty may seem.

known_facts_book1: A little girl from Kansas, made a Princess of Oz by Ozma, who cannot grow big, grow old, or suffer great bodily pain while she lives in the fairyland — but who is still a mortal and could be destroyed or hidden away.
**Starts the whole book by accident**: she is bored by Ozma and Glinda's conversation, wanders to the Great Book of Records, and reads the war notice as the letters are still printing.
Says afterward that she is sorry she noticed the Record — the one line in the book that admits how much trouble one glance cost.
Wears two protections: the Nome King's **Magic Belt** around her waist, and the **Magic Ring** Glinda gives her, to be turned once right and once left only if she is in danger of destruction.
Is attacked by the Spider King and untouched, because of the Belt.
Thinks of the **white crab**: she spots a green crab in a spring pool, and it agrees to cut the purple web in exchange for being made white — the color that purple spiders fear.
Tells Queen Coo-ee-oh she has a pink kitten that talks the same way until it gets a good whipping.
Spends days at a pane of the Dome trying to pick the gold, silver and bronze fishes out of a whole lake of them, and never finds them — the plan is right and the method is hopeless.
**Rings the alarm bell** with Glinda's ring, which is the only reason the Rescue Expedition is ever launched.
Finds the hidden drawer of Gaulau powder by pushing her thumb into a slight hollow in the wall of the Room of Magic.
**Solves the puzzle of the magic words**: Coo-ee-oh used three magic words, and her name is made of three syllables — Coo, ee, oh.
Is the one who sees from the window that 'Coo' has sent all the submarines loose under water.

known_relations_book1.Lady Aurex: Their hostess and keeper under the Dome.
known_relations_book1.Uncle Henry: Her uncle, who joins the Rescue Expedition for her sake.
